phrases.text: So welcome back again.
It's time to solve one more problem.
Now in this problem,
we are given that the ratio of the boat's speed in still water to the stream's speed is five is to one.
Also, the boat takes four hours to travel downstream.
The question is
asking us to find how much time it will take to come back upstream over the same distance.
Hence from ratio,
let the boat speed in still water be
5x and let the stream speed be x. Now we know the formulas.
When boat moves downstream, the current help it to move faster, so downstream speed is boat speed plus
stream speed, and when boat moves upstream, the current opposes it, so upstream speed is boat speed minus stream speed.
So the downstream speed becomes
5x plus x, which is 6x, and the upstream speed becomes 5x minus x, which is 4x.
Done.
Now let us use the downstream journey to find the distance.
Distance is equal to speed multiplied by time.
So distance covered in downstream becomes
6x multiplied by four,
which is 24x.
Now that we know the distance,
finding the upstream time is very easy.
Since the distance covered in both cases are same, so in upstream distance became
24x and the time is equal to distance divided by speed.
So upstream time becomes 24x divided by
The x gets canceled and we get six hours.
Hence,
the boat will take six hours to travel upstream. So the final answer is option C.
